title: Mahalia Jackson: 115 Years Ago Today, the Voice Behind "I Have a Dream" Was Born

lines: Her shout helped King tell the world his dream.
On this day, October 26.
On this day, October twenty-sixth.
115 years ago today, a girl was born in New Orleans.
One hundred and fifteen years ago today, a girl was born in New Orleans.
She would become the Queen of Gospel.
Her name: Mahalia Jackson.
Her name, Mahalia Jackson.

data.hook:
Her shout gave us

data.name: Mahalia

lines: She was born on October 26, 1911, in New Orleans.
She was born on October twenty-sixth, nineteen eleven, in New Orleans.
Her family was poor, and she lost her mother very young.
As a child, she sang in church.
At sixteen, she moved north to Chicago.
People kept telling her to sing the blues.
She always refused.
To her, gospel was the music of hope.

lines: In 1947, one of her gospel songs sold over a million copies.
In nineteen forty-seven, one of her gospel songs sold over a million copies.
It was the best-selling gospel record of its time.
In October 1950, she sang at Carnegie Hall in New York.
In October nineteen fifty, she sang at Carnegie Hall in New York.
In an age of segregation,
Black and white listeners sat side by side to hear her.
She later became the first gospel singer to win a Grammy.
She sang at benefit after benefit to raise money for civil rights.
August 28, 1963: the March on Washington.
August twenty-eighth, nineteen sixty-three: the March on Washington.
A quarter of a million people filled the Lincoln Memorial grounds.
Before Martin Luther King spoke,
she stepped up and sang a spiritual.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 4  Tell them about the dream
lines: King began his speech, reading from his notes.
Then Mahalia called out to him:
"Tell them about the dream, Martin!"
A friend who was there said King pushed his notes aside,
and spoke from the heart: "I have a dream."
In 1968, King was killed, and she sang at his funeral.
In nineteen sixty-eight, King was killed, and she sang at his funeral.
She died near Chicago on January 27, 1972, at sixty.
She died near Chicago on January twenty-seventh, nineteen seventy-two, at sixty.
Tens of thousands of people came to her funeral.
Today she is remembered as the Queen of Gospel.
One honest shout can change a speech, and even an era.
Her question for you:
whose dream around you deserves a push from you?
On this day, October 26,
On this day, October twenty-sixth,
we remember Mahalia Jackson.
